# Upgrade .NET from 8 to 10

## Prerequisites

1. Enable [GitHub Copilot upgrade](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.upgrade-agent), extension ID `ms-dotnettools.upgrade-agent`, in the active VS Code environment. It replaces the deprecated modernization extension. A devcontainer extension entry is desired configuration, not proof that the extension is installed or its tools are exposed.

2. The Dev Container installs SDKs 8 and 10 side by side. Initial setup creates
   a workspace-local `global.json` selecting SDK 8 and `net8.0` projects.
   From `src/workspace/calculator-xunit-testing/`, record `dotnet --version`
   and run `dotnet test calculator.sln` before changing that baseline.
   Verify SDK 10 is available with `dotnet --list-sdks`; a local machine
   missing it can install it from the official
   [.NET website](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0).
   No container image change or rebuild is needed for the upgrade exercise.

3. Inspect the working tree and preserve existing edits. Do not reset files, create commits, or overwrite the workspace to obtain a clean baseline.

4. Familiarize yourself with the [official .NET 10 migration guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/whats-new/dotnet-10/overview).

5. Review the release notes for .NET 10 to understand new features, deprecated APIs, and breaking changes that may affect your project.

6. Ensure all dependencies and NuGet packages used in your project are compatible with .NET 10. Update them to the latest versions if necessary.

7. Reuse the existing xUnit tests and Docker-backed Testcontainers fixture; do not introduce a parallel framework or use a shared local database.

8. Have access to the project files located at "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)\src\workspace\calculator-xunit-testing".

9. Select the **Upgrade** agent or `@upgrade` and discover its actual tools. If unavailable, report the limitation and obtain agreement before substituting a manual upgrade. Do not invent extension commands or claim an extension-native report was generated.

## Task

Upgrade the solution at `src/workspace/calculator-xunit-testing/` from .NET 8
to .NET 10 using the available Upgrade tools. Inspect every existing project:
the initial stage has console/tests, while a later workspace may also have
`calculator.library` and `calculator.web`. An installed SDK 10 does not retarget
`net8.0` projects. If already upgraded, validate instead of recreating projects.

1. Capture `dotnet --info`, `dotnet --list-sdks`, `dotnet --list-runtimes`, actual
   target frameworks, and the baseline test result. Keep intentional .NET 8
   setup/PRD references unchanged. Run baseline commands from inside the
   workspace so its `global.json` selects SDK 8. Reuse an existing `.slnx`
   if this workspace was already upgraded.
2. Update the workspace-local `global.json` to an installed stable SDK 10
   version with a suitable servicing roll-forward policy and verify
   `dotnet --version` from that directory. Use the Upgrade tools to
   retarget all participating projects coherently to `net10.0`. Remove obsolete
   unsupported-framework suppression rather than hiding compatibility failures.
3. Review compatible stable package updates using the package manager. Resolve
   API changes, including the image-taking `PostgreSqlBuilder` constructor,
   without weakening fixture isolation or changing database engines implicitly.
4. Build/test Release, then audit direct and transitive NuGet dependencies.
   Report actual counts and warnings; do not suppress advisories.
   After selecting SDK 10, migrate the initial `.sln` to `.slnx` with
   `dotnet sln src/workspace/calculator-xunit-testing/calculator.sln migrate`.
   Verify the new solution contains every participating project before
   removing the superseded `.sln`. Later prompts use `.slnx`; SDK 8 cannot
   build that format.

   ```bash
   dotnet build src/workspace/calculator-xunit-testing/calculator.slnx --configuration Release
   dotnet test src/workspace/calculator-xunit-testing/calculator.slnx --configuration Release --no-build
   dotnet list src/workspace/calculator-xunit-testing/calculator.slnx package --vulnerable --include-transitive
   ```

5. If the web project exists, validate its .NET 10 static-asset endpoints and
   actual published Release output with the
   `validate-calculator-with-playwright` skill. A Debug server or passing service
   tests alone do not establish published UI readiness.
6. Record framework/package changes, tool provenance, validation results, and
   remaining limitations. Do not provision or deploy Azure resources here.
